title: Remove Methods From Project
statement:
A project has `n` methods, numbered `0` to `n - 1`. Each pair `[a, b]` in `invocations` means that method `a` invokes method `b`.

Method `k` has a known bug. Method `k`, together with every method it invokes directly or through a chain of invocations, is **suspicious**, and you want to remove all suspicious methods. A set of methods can be removed only when no method outside the set invokes a method inside it. If the suspicious methods can be removed this way, remove exactly them; otherwise remove nothing.

Return the methods that remain afterwards, in any order.
constraints: No pair appears twice in invocations
signature: List<Integer> remainingMethods(int n, int k, int[][] invocations)
notes:
## Intuition

Two facts decide the answer: which methods are suspicious, and whether any clean method calls into that group. The first is reachability from `k`, which one depth-first search answers. The second takes one pass over `invocations`: a call `[caller, callee]` blocks the removal exactly when `caller` is clean and `callee` is suspicious. A call leading out of the group cannot exist, since anything a suspicious method calls is suspicious too.

## Approach

1. Build `graph`, the list of methods each method invokes.
2. Mark `k` in `suspicious` and push it on `stack`. Pop a `method`; mark and push each `callee` not marked yet; repeat until the stack is empty.
3. Scan `invocations`. If a clean `caller` invokes a suspicious `callee`, nothing can be removed, so return every method from `0` to `n - 1`.
4. Otherwise collect the clean methods into `remaining` and return it.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 4`, `k = 1`, calls `1 → 2`, `0 → 1` and `3 → 2`. The search from `1` marks `1`, then `2`, so the suspicious group is `{1, 2}`. In the scan, `1 → 2` stays inside the group, but `0 → 1` comes from clean method `0`. The removal is blocked and all methods remain: `[0, 1, 2, 3]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + E), where E is `invocations.length`: building the graph, the search and the scan each touch every method or call a constant number of times.
- Space: O(n + E) for `graph`, `suspicious` and `stack`.

## Pitfalls

- When the removal is blocked, return all `n` methods, not only the clean ones.
- Only calls from outside the group matter; calls between suspicious methods, including cycles back to `k`, are fine.
- A recursive search can overflow the call stack on a long chain of calls; an explicit stack cannot.
- Mark a method when it is pushed, not when it is popped, so it is never pushed twice.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `graph` | `graph[m]` lists the methods that `m` invokes |
| `suspicious` | `suspicious[m]` is true when `m` can be reached from `k` |
| `stack` | suspicious methods whose callees are still to be visited |
| `method` | the method being expanded (later, the method being collected) |
| `caller`, `callee` | the two ends of one invocation |
| `remaining` | the clean methods, returned when the removal is allowed |
